question: What is pneumonia, or lung fever, and what part of the respiratory system does it inflame?
exact_answer_span: Pneumonia, or Lung Fever. This is an inflammation of the substance of the lungs.

question: What are the early symptoms that characterize an acute attack of gastritis?
exact_answer_span: The Early Symptoms of acute gastritis are a burning sensation in the stomach, accompanied by nausea and frequent vomiting.

question: Why is a patient suffering from acute peritonitis compelled to lie on the back in a recumbent position?
exact_answer_span: The patient is compelled to assume a recumbent posture and is inclined to lie on the back, for in that position the sufferer experiences the least pressure of the vital organs against the peritoneum.

question: What are gall-stones and what size variation do they exhibit?
exact_answer_span: These are concretions found in the gall-bladder or bile duct, and vary from the size of a pea to that of a hen's egg.

question: What anatomical condition constitutes prolapsus ani, or falling of the lower bowel?
exact_answer_span: This affection consists of a descent and protrusion of the mucous membrane of the rectum, and, in many cases, of the sub-mucous and muscular coats also.

question: What is the primary diagnostic characteristic of spinal irritation upon clinical examination?
exact_answer_span: Spinal Irritation is characterized by more or less tenderness of the spine, although, in many cases, it is so slight as to pass unnoticed by the patient until pressure is applied.

question: What distinct changes in the color of the eye occur during an attack of acute iritis?
exact_answer_span: There is at first dimness of vision, and the color of the eye is changed; if naturally hazel, it becomes a dark red; if blue or gray, it is changed to a greenish color.

question: What does the term cataract signify when applied to diseases of the eye?
exact_answer_span: The term cataract , when applied to the eye, signifies an opacity of the crystalline lens, or its capsule, or both; the passage of the rays of light being thereby prevented and vision precluded.

question: What does the Greek derivation of alphos signify, and how does the skin eruption present?
exact_answer_span: Alphos , which from its Greek derivation signifies white , is characterized by circular, slightly raised white spots.

question: What preparation is recommended for tightly binding upon a felon in its incipient stage?
exact_answer_span: One of the best preparations that can be used is finely pulverized salt wet with spirits of turpentine, bound tightly upon the affected part and allowed to remain one or two days.

question: Into what five clinical varieties is dysmenorrhea (painful menstruation) divided for description?
exact_answer_span: For convenience of description, dysmenorrhea has been divided into the following varieties: neuralgic , congestive , inflammatory , membranous , and obstructive .

question: What are the two essentially different varieties of diabetes described by medical authorities?
exact_answer_span: There are two essentially different varieties of this disease, one of which is called diabetes insipidus or polyuria , and the other diabetes mellitus , or glycosuria .

question: How does a surgeon definitively detect the presence of a stone in the bladder using an instrument?
exact_answer_span: The surgeon, by exploring the bladder with a steel sound, detects stone with certainty, an audible click being produced when the instrument comes in contact with it.

question: What is the most common cause of organic stricture of the urethra in males?
exact_answer_span: Organic stricture of the urethra generally results from gonorrhea, but may be caused by injuries, sexual excesses, exposure, or by the practice of masturbation, or self-abuse.

question: What anatomical condition constitutes a varicocele, and what does it feel like upon physical examination?
exact_answer_span: Varicocele consists of an enlarged condition of the spermatic veins. In well-marked cases, the veins have a knotted appearance, shown in Fig. 243, and feel much like a bundle or mass of earth-worms.

question: What pathological accumulation of fluid defines dropsy of the scrotum (hydrocele)?
exact_answer_span: This affection consists of a collection of water in the tunica vaginalis , or membranous sac which contains the testicles.

question: What are the three most common varieties of abdominal hernia and which populations are most subject to each?
exact_answer_span: The most common varieties of hernia are umbilical , inguinal , and femoral . Children are most subject to umbilical, males to inguinal, and females to femoral hernia.

question: Into what five general classes are traumatic wounds categorized in surgical practice?
exact_answer_span: Wounds may be classified as incised , punctured , contused , lacerated , or poisoned .

question: What domestic household substances and drinks are recommended as antidotes for iodine poisoning?
exact_answer_span: Starch, wheat flour mixed with water, whites of eggs, milk, and mucilaginous drinks are excellent antidotes.

question: Which organ systems and chronic diseases can be diagnosed with aid from microscopical examination and chemical analysis of the urine?
exact_answer_span: A careful microscopical examination and chemical analysis of the urine is a valuable aid in determining the nature of many chronic diseases, particularly those of the nervous system, blood, liver, kidneys, bladder, prostate gland and generative organs.

question: How does the formation and danger of a false membrane in the larynx in membranous croup compare with when it is confined to the trachea?
exact_answer_span: The formation of this adventitious membrane in the larynx is attended with more danger than when it is confined to the trachea. In most cases in which the disease has had a very speedily fatal termination, an examination has shown that the larynx was its chief seat.

question: What four main causes of jaundice does Professor Da Costa identify in disordered liver conditions?
exact_answer_span: He considers the causes of jaundice to be (1) diseases of the liver; (2) disease of the bile ducts; (3) diseases remote from the liver, or general diseases leading to a disorder of that viscus; (4) certain causes acting upon the blood.

question: What modern medical understanding regarding blood circulation replaces the old practice of blood-letting in apoplexy?
exact_answer_span: Formerly blood-letting was always resorted to in apoplexy, but modern research and observation have proved that this disease is not due to an excess of blood in the system, but to an unequal circulation.

question: What traumatic, mechanical, and medicinal factors are identified as causes of acute inflammation of the kidneys (acute nephritis)?
exact_answer_span: This affection may be caused by injuries, blows upon the back, strains, irritation from calculi, suppressed perspiration, or by the employment of irritating medicines, such as turpentine and cantharides.

question: How does the invention and application of the microscope assist in detecting chronic diseases from urinary samples at the Invalids Hotel?
exact_answer_span: The invention of the microscope has provided increased facilities for detecting diseases by examination of the urine.
